issues.acceptance: A representative native-renderer before/after capture reports raw frame times, one-percent low, hitch count, CPU/GPU attribution, and named script hot paths with 3, 5, 10, and 18 active enemies. Enemy separation is computed once from a cached stable roster per physics cycle, QA instrumentation performs no per-frame deep state snapshot or scene-wide scan in ordinary play, and AI behavior/spacing remains unchanged. llvmpipe evidence is recorded only as collector evidence.
issues.actual: scripts/enemy_agent.gd rebuilds and sorts the complete fusepoint_enemy group inside _separation_safe_velocity(), then invokes that admission path multiple times per navigation cycle for every active enemy. At the same time, the main scene runs RuntimeQualificationProbe in PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, deep-calls mission/roster/weapon state and periodically scans the complete scene tree for audio players. With 18 active enemies these are credible CPU hitch hot paths and must be profiled on a native renderer; the llvmpipe collector result cannot attribute the user's stutter to their computer.
issues.expected: Ordinary gameplay performs bounded enemy steering and lightweight production work per frame; deep QA snapshots run only on demand or at a bounded debug sampling cadence.
issues.next_action: Capture native-renderer CPU/GPU profiler evidence, remove duplicate peer scans and sorts, and gate or sample QA-only deep observation.

stop_conditions: All five host-gated active issue ids are assigned exactly once across the three tasks.
Developer has candidate-owned repairs or fixtures that let Tester run same-loop black-box plus white-box retests for each selected issue.
No task changes retained AK-74M viewmodel source audio, viewmodel transform/profile values, registered map environment tuple, release input bindings, or run-owned evidence/control-plane files.

If a task cannot be fully repaired, it leaves explicit current runtime/source receipts identifying the missing ordinary-input, setup, screenshot, state, log, or mixed-output evidence cell for Tester rather than silently treating source inspection as a pass.

strategy.rationale: The prior two rounds did not reduce active debt enough, so this plan avoids another broad evidence sweep or root transform tweak. It partitions the selected issues by real ownership boundary: HUD/story/effect lifecycle, humanoid animation/root-state binding, and encounter-matrix reachability. The animation task must compare restoration, wrapper/binding repair, replacement, and fixture isolation, then implement a materially different fix from parameter tuning: stop relabeling pistol/neutral clips as rifle states and provide a stable search-state inspection path.

code: Run the project’s available GDScript/static checks for the touched scripts and confirm no parse errors in scripts/tactical_hud.gd, scripts/mission_feedback_controller.gd, scripts/mission_controller.gd, scripts/product_shell.gd, scripts/enemy_roster.gd, systems/actors/humanoid/enemy_humanoid_actor.gd, systems/combat/core/fps_combat_enemy.gd, and systems/combat/core/fps_shot_feedback_3d.gd.
Verify tester_* actions are debug-only, unbound to physical InputMap events in release exports, and record requested/resolved/reset-isolation receipts.
runtime: Clean boot must still pass from title/home through loadout, loading, briefing, deployment, active gameplay, pause/resume, F6 reset, checkpoint recovery when available, Replay, and return Home.

Developer self-validation should use ordinary input first, then tester_prepare actions for Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, enemy search/root tilt, story cue, feedback cleanup, ordinary death, checkpoint restore, and Replay branch cells.

Tester reruns validate:combat_readability_combat_feedback, validate:combat_readability_animation_motion_quality, validate:combat_readability_enemy_combat_ai, and validate:clean_boot with black-box screenshots, runtime_state, scene/tree/spatial state, logs, and receipts.

After firing, impacts, kills, capture/contest, story confirmation, lifecycle cleanup, checkpoint restore, Replay, Home, F6, and tester fixture calls, read late runtime errors and open/update distinct issues for any candidate script callback/backtrace.
visual: At 1280x720 and 200% UI-scale stress, capture gameplay story/radio cues, normal HUD, objective band, combat feed, weapon HUD, and reticle to confirm no clipping, overlap, broad opaque boxed narrative, default-font blockout, or unsafe anchoring; restore/persist 100% UI scale for final matched screenshot.

Capture adjacent-frame enemy samples for both skins across idle, move/search, aim, fire, reload, hurt, death, checkpoint restore, and Replay, including stable actor id, clip, velocity, grounded state, root pitch/roll, muzzle/body facing, and hand/weapon contact.

Capture Alpha, Bravo, and Charlie encounter matrix views that show distributed enemies, full capsule clearance at spawn/restore, reciprocal occlusion for damage authorization, and the 3/5/10 roster coverage in active combat.

done_when: Opening deployment story and radio cues render as concise sentence-case cues in a safe lane at 1280x720 with effective text size at least 36 px, without intersecting countdown, compass, reticle, objective band, combat feed, weapon, enemies, or route view.

Each revealed in-game cue remains readable until explicit Enter or left-click confirmation; the confirmation is consumed by the story system and does not fire the weapon or advance mission authority beyond the presentation layer.
The opening 0-13 second type/hold/fade PRD timing remains observable for deployment while subsequent state-bound radio cues use indefinite post-reveal dwell and one explicit advance receipt per cue.

Feedback effect-token cleanup publishes current receipts showing active_effect_count returns to zero and duplicate_cleanup_callback_count remains zero after fire burst, reload, F6, checkpoint restore, ordinary death/recovery, Replay, and Home without restarting Godot.
HUD/story runtime state exposes layout overlap checks, cue phase, current text, cue index/count, confirmation source, presentation serial, and lifecycle cleanup receipts for Tester.
tasks.instructions: Repair the gameplay story cue and feedback cleanup as one HUD/presentation lifecycle pass. Keep narrative text borderless and integrated with the tactical overlay hierarchy from the PRD visual reference: no opaque subtitle box, debug label, paragraph dump, or permanent prompt. Update story input handling so Enter and left click advance only the presentation cue, with a receipt proving weapon fire was suppressed for that consumed input. Complete the feedback cleanup matrix by routing all transient HUD/VFX/audio effect registrations through one idempotent retirement path and by clearing or retiring tokens on reload, F6, checkpoint restore, death/recovery, Replay, Home, pause/return, and terminal state. Do not create an alternate mission authority or make HUD text the source of truth; all cues observe immutable mission/controller events.

done_when: Live rifle enemies no longer resolve Pistol_Idle, Pistol_Aim_Neutral, Pistol_Shoot, Pistol_Reload, prone/death, or neutral-rest clips for rifle idle, aim, fire, reload, locomotion, hurt, or death states unless explicitly reported as an interim restored baseline that keeps the issue open.

Both shipped enemy skins expose runtime animation receipts with stable actor id, semantic state, resolved clip, weapon family compatibility, normalized time, horizontal velocity, grounded state, muzzle direction, right-hand socket, left-foregrip/stock contact evidence, and alive/dead authority.

Navigation root pitch and roll remain upright through idle, detect/search, move, aim/fire, reload, hurt, death, checkpoint restore, Replay, and F6; the previous search-state tilt window is reachable through ordinary play or a non-release tester_prepare action and has adjacent moving-frame samples.

The implementation compares and records the chosen root-cause strategy among restoring the last visually accepted component baseline, repairing the current wrapper/binding, replacing with one coherent licensed rifle-ready animation set, or isolating missing evidence through fixtures; it does not repeat root-transform tuning as the primary fix.
Attack authorization uses visible body/muzzle facing after ActorRoot plus fixed ModelAxisAdapter correction, never a synthetic marker that disagrees with the rendered rig.
tasks.instructions: Replace the failed clip-label/transform-tuning approach with a binding repair. Inspect the materialized humanoid animation component and the current STATE_CLIPS table; if genuine rifle-ready clips are available locally, bind idle, aim, fire, reload, locomotion, hurt and death to rifle-compatible authored clips with correct loop flags and state authority. If not, restore the last visually accepted stable enemy presentation baseline first to remove prone sliding/root tilt regressions, keep the rifle-semantic issue open in receipts, and prepare a coherent rifle-ready asset intake for a later loop. Keep ActorRoot as the navigation/yaw owner and ModelAxisAdapter as fixed import-axis correction only. Add or repair a debug-only tester_prepare_enemy_search_state fixture that stops in the known failing search pose without killing, capturing, or advancing objectives, and publishes requested/resolved/reset-isolation receipts.

done_when: A current-candidate enemy combat matrix can be executed from one ordinary boot/movement/route smoke plus deterministic non-release branch setup for Alpha, Bravo, and Charlie without arbitrary teleport, noclip, or UI-only state fabrication.

Alpha covers 3 enemies, Bravo covers 5 enemies, and Charlie covers 10 enemies with stable IDs, roles, region activation, alive/dead persistence, perception, movement, cover or route slots, fire, reload, hit reaction, lethal shutdown, and cleanup receipts.

Every tester_prepare encounter action ends in a stable inspectable combat state and has a separate advance/commit action when capture, checkpoint, route opening, death, or terminal transition must be tested.

Enemy spawn and restore receipts prove full capsule clearance, grounded floor/navigation support, nearest-neighbour separation, reserved route/cover slot, and reciprocal static-world occlusion before damage authorization for each sampled stable enemy id.

Checkpoint restore, Replay, F6, and fresh mission preserve enemy identity, position/alive/ammo/activation state, objective state, countdown semantics, and setup reset isolation; no release export exposes tester_* InputMap actions or physical debug bindings.
tasks.instructions: Make fp.domination.progression-unverified directly retestable rather than asking Tester to rediscover unreachable branches. Repair objective/enemy progression blockers that prevent Alpha, Bravo, or Charlie combat coverage, then expose candidate-owned unbound tester_* setup actions for encounter preparation only after ordinary control smoke. Use the same mission, checkpoint, spawn, damage, objective, and terminal APIs as ordinary play. Keep preparation and advancement separate: prepare actions must leave actors alive and inspectable with enough time for screenshots, state sampling, occlusion checks, and animation/audio observation; advance/commit actions may capture points or resolve branch transitions only when that transition is the test subject. Include lifecycle receipts that prove reset isolation and release-build guards.
